generatedProse.concept-context: In a psychology study, research integrity is one thread running from your proposal to your final report. The ethical care you promise when recruiting participants shapes how you store their questionnaire or interview data, which in turn shapes what you can honestly claim in your results. When that thread holds, a reader can trust your findings and you can defend your method.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students run similar studies on memory. One clears the ethics form, then stores raw data on a shared drive and reports results that drift from the approved design. The other sets clear ethical principles, anonymises each participant's data as promised, and keeps the analysis matching the proposal and approval. When a marker probes the method, only the second student can show that integrity held from start to finish.
generatedProse.summary: In your psychology study, integrity is strongest when ethics, data handling and rigour work as one. You carry a single commitment from your proposal to your final report, so each result can be trusted and defended. It is that one practice that makes your research sound.

check.body: A researcher sets ethical principles in the proposal, protects participant data as promised, and keeps the method matching approval right through to the dissertation. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That research integrity is one practice: the same commitment held steady across every stage of the project.
_items.feedback: Yes. Ethics, data and rigour worked as one from start to finish.

_items.text: That the researcher wasted effort by repeating the same check three times.
_items.feedback: These are not repeats. Each strand protects a different part of the same integrity.

_items.text: That only the dissertation stage really matters for integrity.
_items.feedback: Integrity had to hold at every stage, not just the last one.

_items.text: That ethical approval alone guarantees a rigorous project.
_items.feedback: Approval is one step. Rigour is sustained by decisions across the whole project.
